endgames.kind: Rook versus pawns or bare king
Queen versus pawns or bare king
Knight versus pawns or bare king

limitations: Motif detectors are conservative and incomplete; categories overlap.
Opportunity counts are engine-selected screens, not an exhaustive census of all tactics.
Only mate-in-one opportunities are exhaustively checked with legal moves.
Allowed-tactic counts have no equivalent opportunity denominator and should not be compared as miss rates.
Deeper-search errors are checked at finite node budgets, not tablebase truth.
All endgame positions are refined; comparisons below restrict to competitive evaluations and exclude forced mates.
Stable-advantage outcomes can overlap across material categories within a game and are descriptive.
No diagnosis of psychological cause or OTB/rapid skill is made.

evaluation.model: L2 logistic regression implemented with NumPy
evaluation.target: Engine-proxy deterioration of at least 10 percentage points
evaluation.split: Chronological 60 percent train / 20 percent validation / 20 percent test, grouped by whole games
evaluation.scope: Personal bullet play only. Predicts engine-labeled risk, not motives, teaching quality or improvement.
evaluation.label_limitations: Finite-search engine labels are noisy. Evaluation-proxy drops are not calibrated personal win probabilities. Position rows within a game are correlated.

model.scope: Personal bullet play only. Predicts engine-labeled risk, not motives, teaching quality or improvement.

positions.title: Take the hanging queen
positions.explanation: The queen on c3 can be captured with Qxc3. Ke2 instead lets Black check with …b4+ and take the rook on a1 in the checked line.
positions.takeaway: Scan the whole board for undefended pieces before moving your king.

positions.title: Calculate the recapture
positions.explanation: After …Nxd4, Nxd4 is met by …Qxd5. Work through the full exchange rather than rejecting a capture just because the piece can be taken back.
positions.takeaway: Count material after the complete capture sequence.
positions.opening: Vienna Gambit, with Max Lange Defense: Quelle Gambit

positions.title: Look for the finish
positions.explanation: The rook move Rf6 is checkmate. Capturing a pawn with Rxg6 misses an immediate finish. You had 20 seconds, so the position is useful for a deliberate checks-first drill.
positions.takeaway: Before taking material, scan every forcing check.

positions.title: Use the pin before taking the rook
positions.explanation: The pawn on d3 appears to defend the knight on c4, but it is pinned to the king on d2 by the rook on d5. …Qxc4 exploits that alignment. …Qxa1 instead allows Rxa1 and loses the queen.
positions.takeaway: Check which apparent defenders are pinned to their king.

positions.title: Find the mate in two
positions.explanation: Qxf7+ leaves Black only Kh8, followed by Qxg7#. The bishop on b3 protects f7; the bishop on d4 protects g7. Rfd1 misses this sequence.
positions.takeaway: Calculate forcing checks even when the queen moves next to the king.
positions.opening: Sicilian Defense: Modern Variations, Main Line

positions.title: Find the forcing fork
positions.explanation: Nf1+ attacks the king and the rook on d2. The check gives Black time to take the rook in the checked continuation.
positions.takeaway: Look for knight checks that also attack a heavier piece.

positions.title: The queen can fork with check
positions.explanation: …Qd4+ checks the king and attacks the bishop on f4. After Kf1, …Qxf4 collects it. The historical …g5 lets White generate counterplay with Rc8+.
positions.takeaway: A queen check can also be a double attack.

positions.title: Do not check on autopilot
positions.explanation: …Qxg2 is immediate mate. The historical …Nxf3+ lets Qxf3 take the knight. This position carries more than one useful label: missed mate and an allowed free-piece capture.
positions.takeaway: Compare all forcing checks rather than playing the first one you see.

positions.title: Check what the knight can take
positions.explanation: After …Bb7, White has Nxd6, winning the queen even though the knight can be recaptured. …Nxe4 is one checked alternative; several queen retreats also preserve the position.
positions.takeaway: Check the opponent’s captures on your most valuable pieces.
positions.opening: Four Knights Game: Spanish Variation, Classical Variation

positions.title: Stop the mate before taking material
positions.explanation: The historical …axb5 opens the a-file and permits Qa8#. …Qe8 addresses the mating threat. A pawn capture is irrelevant when the king has no escape.
positions.takeaway: Before opening a file, trace the opponent’s queen route to your king.

positions.title: Check the opponent’s jump
positions.explanation: The historical move g6 allowed a knight fork. Practice checking the opponent’s forcing replies before committing to a pawn move.
positions.takeaway: Before your move, scan the opponent’s knight checks.
positions.opening: Vienna Gambit, with Max Lange Defense

positions.title: Step off the fork diagonal
positions.explanation: Qxf5 leaves the king on e1 and rook on a1 exposed to …Qxc3+, a queen fork. Castling first is one sound alternative, moving the king away from the diagonal.
positions.takeaway: Before taking material, check whether your king and rook can be forked.
positions.opening: French Defense: Exchange Variation, Monte Carlo Variation

positions.title: A pawn grab permits a mating net
positions.explanation: After Nxb7, Black has …Rh8+ and the checked line ends Rh4 …Rxh4#. Nf5+ creates a forcing interruption; Rxf7+ is another sound first move.
positions.takeaway: Check the opponent’s rook checks before sending a defender away.

positions.title: Respect the pin on the e-file
positions.explanation: Qb5 allows …Qxb5 because the bishop on e2 is pinned to the king on e1 by the rook on e4. The bishop cannot recapture the queen. Rd2 avoids this tactic.
positions.takeaway: A geometrical defender is not a legal defender when its king is pinned.

positions.title: The pawn can wait
positions.theme: Endgame decision in rook with minor piece material
positions.explanation: Rxd6 releases the black king with …Ke7. Ra7 keeps the rook active on the seventh rank and restricts the king. Compare the lines before deciding that an extra pawn is worth the activity.
positions.takeaway: Ask what your rook is preventing before moving it to take a pawn.

positions.title: Keep the king out of the net
positions.theme: Endgame decision in single rook versus single rook
positions.explanation: After Kg4, the checked line begins …h5+, followed by …g4+ and …g3+. Kh3 avoids that mating net. This is a king-safety decision, even with so little material left.
positions.takeaway: Name the opponent’s strongest pawn check before moving your king.

positions.title: Meet the threat with the rook
positions.theme: Endgame decision in double rook endings
positions.explanation: …Kg8 permits Rag7+ and a sequence of checks that dominates the seventh rank. …Rf7 is the checked defensive resource. Compare the exchange after Raxf7+ before walking the king into the net.
positions.takeaway: Look for an active defensive rook move before retreating the king.

positions.title: Create counterplay with a pawn break
positions.theme: Endgame decision in king and pawn
positions.explanation: …Kf7 allows Kg4 and gives up the favorable evaluation. The checked pawn moves …a4 and …b5 preserve more of Black’s chances. This is a small-sample teaching example, not proof of a general pawn-ending weakness.
positions.takeaway: Calculate pawn breaks alongside king moves in a pawn ending.

positions.title: Remove the obstacle to promotion
positions.theme: Endgame decision in knight versus pawns or bare king
positions.explanation: …Kxa4 removes the a4 pawn and clears a route for the b-pawn. The checked continuation reaches …b1=Q. …Kc3 instead lets the knight reorganize and the evaluation falls to a draw.
positions.takeaway: Identify which pawn blocks your passer, then calculate the promotion race.
positions.opening: Queen's Pawn Game: Accelerated London System

positions.title: A trade changes the whole ending
positions.theme: Endgame decision in single rook versus single rook
positions.explanation: Rxe2+ allows Kxe2 and enters a pawn ending the engine evaluates as losing for Black. Keeping the rooks with Rc3 maintains roughly equal chances.
positions.takeaway: Calculate the pawn ending before offering a rook trade.

transfer.title: Keep the rook against the passer
transfer.explanation: Rc2 puts the rook on the second rank, against the advanced g-pawn. Rc5+ lets Black bring the king to g4 and continue with …g2 in the checked line.
transfer.takeaway: Check which square your rook must control to stop the pawn.
transfer.theme: Endgame decision in single rook versus single rook

transfer.title: Keep the rook active
transfer.explanation: Rd7 threatens the a7-pawn and keeps the rook active. Ra1 lets Black consolidate with …Rc7 in the checked line.
transfer.takeaway: Compare an active rook move with a retreat before choosing defense.
transfer.theme: Endgame decision in single rook versus single rook

transfer.title: Use the forcing resource
transfer.explanation: …Re3+ makes White respond to a check. The historical …Ke7 lets White take the d4-pawn with Rxd4.
transfer.takeaway: Look for a useful check before allowing the opponent to take a pawn.
transfer.theme: Endgame decision in single rook versus single rook

transfer.title: Reposition before the pawns advance
transfer.explanation: Kh3 is the checked king move before Black pushes …d4. The historical h4 commits a pawn while leaving the king on g4. Compare the checked continuations before pushing.
transfer.takeaway: Consider a king move alongside a pawn push.
transfer.theme: Endgame decision in single rook versus single rook

transfer.title: Check before the pawn advances
transfer.explanation: …Rb8+ forces the white king to respond. After the historical …Kd6, White can push b5 and gain the initiative.
transfer.takeaway: Compare a forcing rook check before allowing a passed-pawn advance.
transfer.theme: Endgame decision in single rook versus single rook

transfer.title: Give the rook a target
transfer.explanation: Rh4 targets the d4-pawn; the checked line continues …Rf2, Rxd4. Ra3 instead lets Black play …Ra5 and pressure the a4-pawn.
transfer.takeaway: Choose the rook’s job before choosing its square.
transfer.theme: Endgame decision in single rook versus single rook
